a0692.reason: The body said that from 153 BC 'January became the first month of the year'. Roman writers place January at the head of the calendar much earlier (under Numa or the Decemvirs, c. 450 BC); what changed in 153 BC is that the consuls entered office on 1 January (Livy, Periochae 47.13), so 1 January became the start of the official (consular) year. Sentence reworded in EN/DE/RU.

f20361.reason: Timeline label said 1 January became 'the first day of the year'; narrowed to 'the first day of the official year' (the consular year), matching Livy, Periochae 47.13 and the corrected body.
